metaTitle: Outlet Not Working in Los Angeles? Repair Cost & Causes
metaDescription: A dead outlet in your LA home could mean a tripped GFCI, bad wiring, or an overloaded circuit. See likely causes, what a pro does, and the real price range.
intro: Flipping a switch and getting nothing from an outlet is one of the more common electrical complaints in Los Angeles, where pre-war bungalows, mid-century houses, and newer apartment buildings all wire things a little differently. Sometimes it's a simple reset; other times it points to aging wiring behind the wall that shouldn't be ignored.
causes: A tripped GFCI outlet somewhere on the same circuit (often in a bathroom or kitchen) has cut power to other outlets downstream, which is common in older bungalows retrofitted with only one or two GFCI points.
A breaker has tripped in the panel, which happens more often in mid-century homes where the original electrical panel was sized for far fewer appliances than people run today.
Loose or corroded wiring connections at the outlet itself, a frequent issue in pre-war housing stock where cloth or aluminum wiring may still be present.
A worn-out outlet with broken internal contacts, which is common in rental apartments that see high tenant turnover and years of plugging and unplugging.
A break somewhere in the wiring run between the panel and the outlet, which is harder to spot and more likely in homes that have been partially remodeled over the decades.
whatProDoes: Checks the breaker panel and any GFCI outlets on the same circuit first, since resetting one of these solves the problem in many cases.
Tests the outlet with a multimeter to confirm whether power is actually reaching it and whether the issue is the outlet or the wiring feeding it.
Opens the outlet box to inspect for loose, burnt, or corroded connections, which is especially important in older LA homes with original wiring.
Traces the circuit to locate a break or fault if the problem isn't at the outlet itself, sometimes checking other outlets on the same run.
Replaces the outlet or repairs the connection, then re-tests to confirm power is restored safely.
diyOrPro: Checking your breaker panel and pressing the reset button on any nearby GFCI outlets is safe to try yourself and fixes the issue a fair amount of the time. Opening the outlet, touching wires, or troubleshooting anything beyond a simple reset is not something to attempt yourself, since misdiagnosing a wiring fault or working on a live circuit can cause a shock or start a fire.
priceNote: This job runs $135 to $235 in Los Angeles, based on a $100/hour rate for a typical 1-2 hour visit. The time depends mostly on whether the fix is a quick outlet swap or a longer trace-and-repair through walls in an older property.

faqs.q: Why does only one outlet in the room not work while the others are fine?
faqs.a: Outlets are often wired in a chain, so if one in the middle fails or a GFCI outlet upstream trips, everything after it on that chain loses power even though nearby outlets on a different circuit stay on.

faqs.q: Is it dangerous to leave a dead outlet alone if I don't need it?
faqs.a: It can be. A dead outlet sometimes signals a loose connection that's overheating behind the wall, so it's worth having it checked even if you're not currently using that outlet.

faqs.q: Will resetting my breaker fix it for good?
faqs.a: If a tripped breaker was the whole problem, resetting it can work permanently, but if it trips again soon after, that usually means there's an underlying fault that needs a professional to find and fix.
